L0:       SUBROUTINE 【0†DGELSY】( M, N, NRHS, A, LDA, B, LDB, JPVT, RCOND, RANK,
L1:          $                   WORK, LWORK, INFO )
L2:     *
L3:     *  -- LAPACK driver routine (version 3.1) --
L4:     *     Univ. of Tennessee, Univ. of California Berkeley and NAG Ltd..
L5:     *     November 2006
L6:     *
L7:     *     .. Scalar Arguments ..
L8:           INTEGER            INFO, LDA, LDB, LWORK, M, N, NRHS, RANK
L9:           DOUBLE PRECISION   RCOND
L10:     *     ..
L11:     *     .. Array Arguments ..
L12:           INTEGER            JPVT( * )
L13:           DOUBLE PRECISION   A( LDA, * ), B( LDB, * ), WORK( * )
L14:     *     ..
L15:     *
L16:     *  Purpose
L17:     *  =======
L18:     *
L19:     *  【0†DGELSY】 computes the minimum-norm solution to a real linear least
L20:     *  squares problem:
L21:     *      minimize || A * X - B ||
L22:     *  using a complete orthogonal factorization of A.  A is an M-by-N
L23:     *  matrix which may be rank-deficient.
L24:     *
L25:     *  Several right hand side vectors b and solution vectors x can be
L26:     *  handled in a single call; they are stored as the columns of the
L27:     *  M-by-NRHS right hand side matrix B and the N-by-NRHS solution
L28:     *  matrix X.
L29:     *
L30:     *  The routine first computes a QR factorization with column pivoting:
L31:     *      A * P = Q * [ R11 R12 ]
L32:     *                  [  0  R22 ]
L33:     *  with R11 defined as the largest leading submatrix whose estimated
L34:     *  condition number is less than 1/RCOND.  The order of R11, RANK,
L35:     *  is the effective rank of A.
L36:     *
L37:     *  Then, R22 is considered to be negligible, and R12 is annihilated
L38:     *  by orthogonal transformations from the right, arriving at the
L39:     *  complete orthogonal factorization:
L40:     *     A * P = Q * [ T11 0 ] * Z
L41:     *                 [  0  0 ]
L42:     *  The minimum-norm solution is then
L43:     *     X = P * Z' [ inv(T11)*Q1'*B ]
L44:     *                [        0       ]
L45:     *  where Q1 consists of the first RANK columns of Q.
L46:     *
L47:     *  This routine is basically identical to the original xGELSX except
L48:     *  three differences:
L49:     *    o The call to the subroutine xGEQPF has been substituted by the
L50:     *      the call to the subroutine xGEQP3. This subroutine is a Blas-3
L51:     *      version of the QR factorization with column pivoting.
L52:     *    o Matrix B (the right hand side) is updated with Blas-3.
L53:     *    o The permutation of matrix B (the right hand side) is faster and
L54:     *      more simple.
L55:     *
L56:     *  Arguments
L57:     *  =========
L58:     *
L59:     *  M       (input) INTEGER
L60:     *          The number of rows of the matrix A.  M >= 0.
L61:     *
L62:     *  N       (input) INTEGER
L63:     *          The number of columns of the matrix A.  N >= 0.
L64:     *
L65:     *  NRHS    (input) INTEGER
L66:     *          The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of
L67:     *          columns of matrices B and X. NRHS >= 0.
L68:     *
L69:     *  A       (input/output) DOUBLE PRECISION array, dimension (LDA,N)
L70:     *          On entry, the M-by-N matrix A.
L71:     *          On exit, A has been overwritten by details of its
L72:     *          complete orthogonal factorization.
L73:     *
L74:     *  LDA     (input) INTEGER
L75:     *          The leading dimension of the array A.  LDA >= max(1,M).
L76:     *
L77:     *  B       (input/output) DOUBLE PRECISION array, dimension (LDB,NRHS)
L78:     *          On entry, the M-by-NRHS right hand side matrix B.
L79:     *          On exit, the N-by-NRHS solution matrix X.
L80:     *
L81:     *  LDB     (input) INTEGER
L82:     *          The leading dimension of the array B. LDB >= max(1,M,N).
L83:     *
L84:     *  JPVT    (input/output) INTEGER array, dimension (N)
L85:     *          On entry, if JPVT(i) .ne. 0, the i-th column of A is permuted
L86:     *          to the front of AP, otherwise column i is a free column.
L87:     *          On exit, if JPVT(i) = k, then the i-th column of AP
L88:     *          was the k-th column of A.
L89:     *
L90:     *  RCOND   (input) DOUBLE PRECISION
L91:     *          RCOND is used to determine the effective rank of A, which
L92:     *          is defined as the order of the largest leading triangular
L93:     *          submatrix R11 in the QR factorization with pivoting of A,
L94:     *          whose estimated condition number < 1/RCOND.
L95:     *
L96:     *  RANK    (output) INTEGER
L97:     *          The effective rank of A, i.e., the order of the submatrix
L98:     *          R11.  This is the same as the order of the submatrix T11
L99:     *          in the complete orthogonal factorization of A.
L100:     *
L101:     *  WORK    (workspace/output) DOUBLE PRECISION array, dimension (MAX(1,LWORK))
L102:     *          On exit, if INFO = 0, WORK(1) returns the optimal LWORK.
L103:     *
L104:     *  LWORK   (input) INTEGER
L105:     *          The dimension of the array WORK.
L106:     *          The unblocked strategy requires that:
L107:     *             LWORK >= MAX( MN+3*N+1, 2*MN+NRHS ),
L108:     *          where MN = min( M, N ).
L109:     *          The block algorithm requires that:
L110:     *             LWORK >= MAX( MN+2*N+NB*(N+1), 2*MN+NB*NRHS ),
L111:     *          where NB is an upper bound on the blocksize returned
L112:     *          by 【1†ILAENV】 for the routines 【2†DGEQP3】, 【3†DTZRZF】, 【4†STZRQF】, 【5†DORMQR】,
L113:     *          and 【6†DORMRZ】.
L114:     *
L115:     *          If LWORK = -1, then a workspace query is assumed; the routine
L116:     *          only calculates the optimal size of the WORK array, returns
L117:     *          this value as the first entry of the WORK array, and no error
L118:     *          message related to LWORK is issued by 【7†XERBLA】.
L119:     *
L120:     *  INFO    (output) INTEGER
L121:     *          = 0: successful exit
L122:     *          < 0: If INFO = -i, the i-th argument had an illegal value.
L123:     *
L124:     *  Further Details
L125:     *  ===============
L126:     *
L127:     *  Based on contributions by
L128:     *    A. Petitet, Computer Science Dept., Univ. of Tenn., Knoxville, USA
L129:     *    E. Quintana-Orti, Depto. de Informatica, Universidad Jaime I, Spain
L130:     *    G. Quintana-Orti, Depto. de Informatica, Universidad Jaime I, Spain
L131:     *
L132:     *  =====================================================================
L133:     *
L134:     *     .. Parameters ..
L135:           INTEGER            IMAX, IMIN
L136:           PARAMETER          ( IMAX = 1, IMIN = 2 )
L137:           DOUBLE PRECISION   ZERO, ONE
L138:           PARAMETER          ( ZERO = 0.0D+0, ONE = 1.0D+0 )
L139:     *     ..
L140:     *     .. Local Scalars ..
L141:           LOGICAL            LQUERY
L142:           INTEGER            I, IASCL, IBSCL, ISMAX, ISMIN, J, LWKMIN,
L143:          $                   LWKOPT, MN, NB, NB1, NB2, NB3, NB4
L144:           DOUBLE PRECISION   ANRM, BIGNUM, BNRM, C1, C2, S1, S2, SMAX,
L145:          $                   SMAXPR, SMIN, SMINPR, SMLNUM, WSIZE
L146:     *     ..
L147:     *     .. External Functions ..
L148:           INTEGER            【1†ILAENV】
L149:           DOUBLE PRECISION   【8†DLAMCH】, 【9†DLANGE】
L150:           EXTERNAL           【1†ILAENV】, 【8†DLAMCH】, 【9†DLANGE】
L151:     *     ..
L152:     *     .. External Subroutines ..
L153:           EXTERNAL           DCOPY, 【2†DGEQP3】, 【10†DLABAD】, 【11†DLAIC1】, 【12†DLASCL】, 【13†DLASET】,
L154:          $                   【5†DORMQR】, 【6†DORMRZ】, DTRSM, 【3†DTZRZF】, 【7†XERBLA】
L155:     *     ..
L156:     *     .. Intrinsic Functions ..
L157:           INTRINSIC          ABS, MAX, MIN
L158:     *     ..
L159:     *     .. Executable Statements ..
L160:     *
L161:           MN = MIN( M, N )
L162:           ISMIN = MN + 1
L163:           ISMAX = 2*MN + 1
L164:     *
L165:     *     Test the input arguments.
L166:     *
L167:           INFO = 0
L168:           LQUERY = ( LWORK.EQ.-1 )
L169:           IF( M.LT.0 ) THEN
L170:              INFO = -1
L171:           ELSE IF( N.LT.0 ) THEN
L172:              INFO = -2
L173:           ELSE IF( NRHS.LT.0 ) THEN
L174:              INFO = -3
L175:           ELSE IF( LDA.LT.MAX( 1, M ) ) THEN
L176:              INFO = -5
L177:           ELSE IF( LDB.LT.MAX( 1, M, N ) ) THEN
L178:              INFO = -7
L179:           END IF
L180:     *
L181:     *     Figure out optimal block size
L182:     *
L183:           IF( INFO.EQ.0 ) THEN
L184:              IF( MN.EQ.0 .OR. NRHS.EQ.0 ) THEN
L185:                 LWKMIN = 1
L186:                 LWKOPT = 1
L187:              ELSE
L188:                 NB1 = 【1†ILAENV】( 1, '【14†DGEQRF】', ' ', M, N, -1, -1 )
L189:                 NB2 = 【1†ILAENV】( 1, '【15†DGERQF】', ' ', M, N, -1, -1 )
L190:                 NB3 = 【1†ILAENV】( 1, '【5†DORMQR】', ' ', M, N, NRHS, -1 )
L191:                 NB4 = 【1†ILAENV】( 1, '【16†DORMRQ】', ' ', M, N, NRHS, -1 )
L192:                 NB = MAX( NB1, NB2, NB3, NB4 )
L193:                 LWKMIN = MN + MAX( 2*MN, N + 1, MN + NRHS )
L194:                 LWKOPT = MAX( LWKMIN,
L195:          $                    MN + 2*N + NB*( N + 1 ), 2*MN + NB*NRHS )
L196:              END IF
L197:              WORK( 1 ) = LWKOPT
L198:     *
L199:              IF( LWORK.LT.LWKMIN .AND. .NOT.LQUERY ) THEN
L200:                 INFO = -12
L201:              END IF
L202:           END IF
L203:     *
L204:           IF( INFO.NE.0 ) THEN
L205:              CALL 【7†XERBLA】( '【0†DGELSY】', -INFO )
L206:              RETURN
L207:           ELSE IF( LQUERY ) THEN
L208:              RETURN
L209:           END IF
L210:     *
L211:     *     Quick return if possible
L212:     *
L213:           IF( MN.EQ.0 .OR. NRHS.EQ.0 ) THEN
L214:              RANK = 0
L215:              RETURN
L216:           END IF
L217:     *
L218:     *     Get machine parameters
L219:     *
L220:           SMLNUM = 【8†DLAMCH】( 'S' ) / 【8†DLAMCH】( 'P' )
L221:           BIGNUM = ONE / SMLNUM
L222:           CALL 【10†DLABAD】( SMLNUM, BIGNUM )
L223:     *
L224:     *     Scale A, B if max entries outside range [SMLNUM,BIGNUM]
L225:     *
L226:           ANRM = 【9†DLANGE】( 'M', M, N, A, LDA, WORK )
L227:           IASCL = 0
L228:           IF( ANRM.GT.ZERO .AND. ANRM.LT.SMLNUM ) THEN
L229:     *
L230:     *        Scale matrix norm up to SMLNUM
L231:     *
L232:              CALL 【12†DLASCL】( 'G', 0, 0, ANRM, SMLNUM, M, N, A, LDA, INFO )
L233:              IASCL = 1
L234:           ELSE IF( ANRM.GT.BIGNUM ) THEN
L235:     *
L236:     *        Scale matrix norm down to BIGNUM
L237:     *
L238:              CALL 【12†DLASCL】( 'G', 0, 0, ANRM, BIGNUM, M, N, A, LDA, INFO )
L239:              IASCL = 2
L240:           ELSE IF( ANRM.EQ.ZERO ) THEN
L241:     *
L242:     *        Matrix all zero. Return zero solution.
L243:     *
L244:              CALL 【13†DLASET】( 'F', MAX( M, N ), NRHS, ZERO, ZERO, B, LDB )
L245:              RANK = 0
L246:              GO TO 70
L247:           END IF
L248:     *
L249:           BNRM = 【9†DLANGE】( 'M', M, NRHS, B, LDB, WORK )
L250:           IBSCL = 0
L251:           IF( BNRM.GT.ZERO .AND. BNRM.LT.SMLNUM ) THEN
L252:     *
L253:     *        Scale matrix norm up to SMLNUM
L254:     *
L255:              CALL 【12†DLASCL】( 'G', 0, 0, BNRM, SMLNUM, M, NRHS, B, LDB, INFO )
L256:              IBSCL = 1
L257:           ELSE IF( BNRM.GT.BIGNUM ) THEN
L258:     *
L259:     *        Scale matrix norm down to BIGNUM
L260:     *
L261:              CALL 【12†DLASCL】( 'G', 0, 0, BNRM, BIGNUM, M, NRHS, B, LDB, INFO )
L262:              IBSCL = 2
L263:           END IF
L264:     *
L265:     *     Compute QR factorization with column pivoting of A:
L266:     *        A * P = Q * R
L267:     *
L268:           CALL 【2†DGEQP3】( M, N, A, LDA, JPVT, WORK( 1 ), WORK( MN+1 ),
L269:          $             LWORK-MN, INFO )
L270:           WSIZE = MN + WORK( MN+1 )
L271:     *
L272:     *     workspace: MN+2*N+NB*(N+1).
L273:     *     Details of Householder rotations stored in WORK(1:MN).
L274:     *
L275:     *     Determine RANK using incremental condition estimation
L276:     *
L277:           WORK( ISMIN ) = ONE
L278:           WORK( ISMAX ) = ONE
L279:           SMAX = ABS( A( 1, 1 ) )
L280:           SMIN = SMAX
L281:           IF( ABS( A( 1, 1 ) ).EQ.ZERO ) THEN
L282:              RANK = 0
L283:              CALL 【13†DLASET】( 'F', MAX( M, N ), NRHS, ZERO, ZERO, B, LDB )
L284:              GO TO 70
L285:           ELSE
L286:              RANK = 1
L287:           END IF
L288:     *
L289:        10 CONTINUE
L290:           IF( RANK.LT.MN ) THEN
L291:              I = RANK + 1
L292:              CALL 【11†DLAIC1】( IMIN, RANK, WORK( ISMIN ), SMIN, A( 1, I ),
L293:          $                A( I, I ), SMINPR, S1, C1 )
L294:              CALL 【11†DLAIC1】( IMAX, RANK, WORK( ISMAX ), SMAX, A( 1, I ),
L295:          $                A( I, I ), SMAXPR, S2, C2 )
L296:     *
L297:              IF( SMAXPR*RCOND.LE.SMINPR ) THEN
L298:                 DO 20 I = 1, RANK
L299:                    WORK( ISMIN+I-1 ) = S1*WORK( ISMIN+I-1 )
L300:                    WORK( ISMAX+I-1 ) = S2*WORK( ISMAX+I-1 )
L301:        20       CONTINUE
L302:                 WORK( ISMIN+RANK ) = C1
L303:                 WORK( ISMAX+RANK ) = C2
L304:                 SMIN = SMINPR
L305:                 SMAX = SMAXPR
L306:                 RANK = RANK + 1
L307:                 GO TO 10
L308:              END IF
L309:           END IF
L310:     *
L311:     *     workspace: 3*MN.
L312:     *
L313:     *     Logically partition R = [ R11 R12 ]
L314:     *                             [  0  R22 ]
L315:     *     where R11 = R(1:RANK,1:RANK)
L316:     *
L317:     *     [R11,R12] = [ T11, 0 ] * Y
L318:     *
L319:           IF( RANK.LT.N )
L320:          $   CALL 【3†DTZRZF】( RANK, N, A, LDA, WORK( MN+1 ), WORK( 2*MN+1 ),
L321:          $                LWORK-2*MN, INFO )
L322:     *
L323:     *     workspace: 2*MN.
L324:     *     Details of Householder rotations stored in WORK(MN+1:2*MN)
L325:     *
L326:     *     B(1:M,1:NRHS) := Q' * B(1:M,1:NRHS)
L327:     *
L328:           CALL 【5†DORMQR】( 'Left', 'Transpose', M, NRHS, MN, A, LDA, WORK( 1 ),
L329:          $             B, LDB, WORK( 2*MN+1 ), LWORK-2*MN, INFO )
L330:           WSIZE = MAX( WSIZE, 2*MN+WORK( 2*MN+1 ) )
L331:     *
L332:     *     workspace: 2*MN+NB*NRHS.
L333:     *
L334:     *     B(1:RANK,1:NRHS) := inv(T11) * B(1:RANK,1:NRHS)
L335:     *
L336:           CALL DTRSM( 'Left', 'Upper', 'No transpose', 'Non-unit', RANK,
L337:          $            NRHS, ONE, A, LDA, B, LDB )
L338:     *
L339:           DO 40 J = 1, NRHS
L340:              DO 30 I = RANK + 1, N
L341:                 B( I, J ) = ZERO
L342:        30    CONTINUE
L343:        40 CONTINUE
L344:     *
L345:     *     B(1:N,1:NRHS) := Y' * B(1:N,1:NRHS)
L346:     *
L347:           IF( RANK.LT.N ) THEN
L348:              CALL 【6†DORMRZ】( 'Left', 'Transpose', N, NRHS, RANK, N-RANK, A,
L349:          $                LDA, WORK( MN+1 ), B, LDB, WORK( 2*MN+1 ),
L350:          $                LWORK-2*MN, INFO )
L351:           END IF
L352:     *
L353:     *     workspace: 2*MN+NRHS.
L354:     *
L355:     *     B(1:N,1:NRHS) := P * B(1:N,1:NRHS)
L356:     *
L357:           DO 60 J = 1, NRHS
L358:              DO 50 I = 1, N
L359:                 WORK( JPVT( I ) ) = B( I, J )
L360:        50    CONTINUE
L361:              CALL DCOPY( N, WORK( 1 ), 1, B( 1, J ), 1 )
L362:        60 CONTINUE
L363:     *
L364:     *     workspace: N.
L365:     *
L366:     *     Undo scaling
L367:     *
L368:           IF( IASCL.EQ.1 ) THEN
L369:              CALL 【12†DLASCL】( 'G', 0, 0, ANRM, SMLNUM, N, NRHS, B, LDB, INFO )
L370:              CALL 【12†DLASCL】( 'U', 0, 0, SMLNUM, ANRM, RANK, RANK, A, LDA,
L371:          $                INFO )
L372:           ELSE IF( IASCL.EQ.2 ) THEN
L373:              CALL 【12†DLASCL】( 'G', 0, 0, ANRM, BIGNUM, N, NRHS, B, LDB, INFO )
L374:              CALL 【12†DLASCL】( 'U', 0, 0, BIGNUM, ANRM, RANK, RANK, A, LDA,
L375:          $                INFO )
L376:           END IF
L377:           IF( IBSCL.EQ.1 ) THEN
L378:              CALL 【12†DLASCL】( 'G', 0, 0, SMLNUM, BNRM, N, NRHS, B, LDB, INFO )
L379:           ELSE IF( IBSCL.EQ.2 ) THEN
L380:              CALL 【12†DLASCL】( 'G', 0, 0, BIGNUM, BNRM, N, NRHS, B, LDB, INFO )
L381:           END IF
L382:     *
L383:        70 CONTINUE
L384:           WORK( 1 ) = LWKOPT
L385:     *
L386:           RETURN
L387:     *
L388:     *     End of 【0†DGELSY】
L389:     *
L390:           END

L2: Linear Least Squares (LLS) Problems
L3: 
L4: The linear least squares problem is:
L5: 
L6: 【5†Image: \begin{displaymath} \mathop{\mbox{minimize }}_{x} \Vert b - A x {\Vert}_2 \end{displaymath}】  | (2.1)
L7: 
L8: where A is an m-by-n matrix, b is a given m element vector and x is the n element solution vector.
L9: In the most usual case 【6†Image: $m \ge n$】 and 【7†Image: $\mbox{rank}(A) = n$】, and in this case the solution to problem (【8†2.1】) is unique, and the problem is also referred to as finding a least squares solution to an overdetermined system of linear equations.
L10: When m < n and 【9†Image: $\mbox{rank}(A) = m$】, there are an infinite number of solutions x which exactly satisfy b-Ax=0. In this case it is often useful to find the unique solution x which minimizes |x|_{2}, and the problem is referred to as finding a minimum norm solution to an underdetermined system of linear equations.
L11: The driver routine xGELS solves problem (【8†2.1】) on the assumption that 【10†Image: $\mbox{rank}(A) = \min(m,n)$】 -- in other words, A has full rank -- finding a least squares solution of an overdetermined system when m > n, and a minimum norm solution of an underdetermined system when m < n. xGELS uses a QR or LQ factorization of A, and also allows A to be replaced by A^{T} in the statement of the problem (or by A^{H} if A is complex).
L12: In the general case when we may have 【11†Image: $\mbox{rank}(A) < \min(m,n)$】 -- in other words, A may be rank-deficient -- we seek the minimum norm least squares solution x which minimizes both |x|_{2} and 【12†Image: $\Vert b - Ax{\Vert}_2$】.
L13: The driver routines xGELSX, xGELSY, xGELSS, and xGELSD, solve this general formulation of problem 【8†2.1】, allowing for the possibility that A is rank-deficient; xGELSX and xGELSY use a complete orthogonal factorization of A, while xGELSS uses the singular value decomposition of A, and xGELSD uses the singular value decomposition of A with an algorithm based on divide and conquer.
L14: The subroutine xGELSY is a faster version of xGELSX, but requires more workspace since it calls blocked algorithms to perform the complete orthogonal factorization. xGELSX has been retained for compatibility with Release 2.0 of LAPACK, but we omit references to this routine in the remainder of this users' guide.
L15: 
L16: The subroutine xGELSD is significantly faster than its older counterpart xGELSS, especially for large problems, but may require somewhat more workspace depending on the matrix dimensions.
L17: The LLS driver routines are listed in Table 【13†2.3】.
L18: 
L19: All four routines allow several right hand side vectors b and corresponding solutions x to be handled in a single call, storing these vectors as columns of matrices B and X, respectively. Note however that problem 【8†2.1】 is solved for each right hand side vector independently; this is not the same as finding a matrix X which minimizes 【14†Image: $\Vert B - A X \Vert _2$】.
L20: Table 2.3: Driver routines for linear least squares problems
L21: Operation  | Single precision  | Double precision
L22:    | real  | complex  | real  | complex
L23: solve LLS using QR or LQ factorization  | SGELS  | CGELS  | DGELS  | ZGELS
